name: Winamax
industry: online poker and sports betting operator
desc: French online gambling operator offering poker, sports betting and horse racing betting to players in France and Spain.
capacity_detail: Revenue (chiffre d'affaires) EUR 744m in 2023, up from EUR 643m in 2022, per filed-accounts summary
sponsorships: VfB Stuttgart sponsor (2023, ended early 2025); ES Troyes AC shirt sponsor (2022-23); RC Strasbourg (2020); Granada CF shirt sponsor (2019-20)
markets: France as home market; also Spain; history of football club sponsorships in France, Spain and Germany.
rationale: Heavy football sponsor in France, Spain and Germany seeking premium sports visibility; F1's young French and Spanish audiences fit its poker and betting brand.

name: VBET
industry: online sports betting and casino operator
desc: International online sports betting and gaming operator, a subsidiary of the SoftConstruct group, sponsoring European football clubs.
capacity_detail: Official sports betting partner of Ligue 1 club AS Monaco since 2020, extended in March 2025 until 2029 (shorts and training kit branding)
sponsorships: AS Monaco official sports betting partner (2020-2029); OGC Nice partner (extended to 2028); Botafogo shirt sponsor (2025-2027)
markets: Online betting across Europe and the Americas; sponsors football and hockey clubs, leagues and federations in Europe and America.
rationale: Already invested in Monaco, home of a Grand Prix; F1 would extend its European and Latin American sponsorship strategy to a global stage.

name: Caliente
desc: Mexican sports betting and gaming company operating the Caliente.mx online sportsbook and a major sports sponsorship programme.
capacity_detail: Official sponsor of the NBA in Mexico under a three-year agreement announced October 2026
sponsorships: NBA official sponsor in Mexico (2026, three years); Concacaf Champions Cup and W Champions Cup official sponsor in Mexico (2026-2027); Concacaf Gold Cup sponsor (2025); Mexico national team partner (from 2023)
markets: Mexico, where it runs the Caliente.mx sportsbook and sponsors national team, Concacaf and NBA properties.
rationale: Its commercial director says Caliente is exploring Formula 1; the Mexico City Grand Prix offers a direct home-market activation for a growing sports sponsor.

name: Tipsport
desc: Czech betting company offering sports betting and gaming online and through branches, the largest bookmaker in its home market.
capacity_detail: Tipsport.net revenue CZK 15.15bn in 2024 (up 12%), net profit CZK 3.36bn, per its annual report (about USD 650m at roughly CZK 23 per USD)
sponsorships: Former sponsor of the Czech and Slovak ice hockey Extraliga; arena naming rights
markets: Czech Republic and Slovakia, online and retail betting; sister brands Chance and Maxa in the same group.
rationale: Highly profitable Central European bookmaker with large sponsorship budgets; F1 hospitality and content could extend its premium sports positioning beyond hockey and football.

name: STARTRADER
desc: Online multi-asset broker offering forex and CFD trading through regulated entities in several jurisdictions worldwide.
capacity_detail: Official Partner of the NBA, shown on the broker's sponsorship page
sponsorships: NBA official partner; Porsche Carrera Cup Middle East official partner; ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026; UAE national cricket team; PFL Champions Series
markets: Regulated entities in South Africa, Seychelles, Mauritius, Cyprus and the UK serving retail traders internationally.
rationale: Sponsorship-led broker already backing the NBA and Porsche motorsport; peers such as Pepperstone, IC Markets and XMTrading are F1 partners.

name: Doo Group
desc: Global financial services group with fintech at its core, offering online trading through entities holding over 20 licences.
capacity_detail: Official Online Financial Trading Platform Partner of Manchester United (Premier League), shown on the group's website
sponsorships: Manchester United official online financial trading platform partner; Adelaide United partner
markets: Clients in 150+ countries and regions, with 20+ global operation centres and 400,000+ clients.
rationale: Already pays for Premier League visibility; F1 would match rival brokers Pepperstone, IC Markets and XMTrading on a truly global platform.

name: Questrade
desc: Canadian online brokerage and wealth management firm offering self-directed trading, managed portfolios and, more recently, banking services.
capacity_detail: Reported to generate over USD 300m in annual revenue (Globe and Mail, late 2024); president said current sales are substantially greater
markets: Canada: self-directed investing, managed portfolios and a newly licensed bank; over CAD 85bn in assets.
rationale: Self-funded, profitable challenger to Canada's big banks; the Canadian Grand Prix and F1's growing Canadian fan base suit its brand-building.

name: Mimecast
desc: Cybersecurity company providing cloud email security, archiving and human-risk protection for organisations, owned by private equity firm Permira.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 501.4m in the fiscal year to March 2021, per its last 10-K before the 2022 Permira takeover
markets: Global HQ in London and North America HQ in Lexington, Massachusetts; serves organisations worldwide.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers like CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Bitdefender use F1 for B2B hospitality; Mimecast's UK base and enterprise customers suit that model.

name: Barracuda Networks
desc: Security company providing email protection, network security, application security and data protection, owned by KKR since 2022.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 352.6m in the fiscal year to February 2017 per its 10-K; bought by KKR for about USD 4bn in 2022
markets: Security products sold to businesses and managed service providers worldwide from its Campbell, California base.
rationale: Mid-market security vendor competing with F1-backed peers like CrowdStrike and Cato Networks; F1 offers partner and customer hospitality at scale.

name: BeyondTrust
desc: Identity security company providing privileged access management and remote access software, backed by Francisco Partners since 2018.
capacity_detail: Generates around USD 500m in annual recurring revenue, reported August 2025 as Francisco Partners explored a sale
markets: Identity security software for enterprises worldwide; based in Johns Creek, Georgia, with Clearlake as minority investor.
rationale: Identity security rivals Okta, Keeper Security and 1Password are F1 partners; BeyondTrust could match them in enterprise brand awareness.

name: SK Shieldus
desc: South Korean security company providing cybersecurity, physical security, facility management and unmanned store solutions, acquired by EQT in 2023.
capacity_detail: Revenue about KRW 2.0047 trillion in 2024 with operating profit of about KRW 141.6bn, per its 2025 sustainability report (about USD 1.47bn)
markets: South Korea: cyber and physical security, facility management and unmanned store solutions for businesses and homes.
rationale: Large Korean security brand under EQT ownership; F1 could support B2B profile building, though its business is mainly domestic.
